events.text: Your first word is 'more', said very firmly to an empty rice bowl. The family adopts it as a motto.
You crawl out of the house, across the yard and halfway up the chicken coop before anyone notices. The chickens have not forgiven you.
Your father sits you at the counting table with an abacus. 'A merchant's child must count before they can walk properly.'

effects.log: By the end of the season you catch a clerk shaving copper off every sale. Your father is so proud he nearly cries.

choices.text: Use the abacus as a sword

effects.log: The beads go everywhere. You are sent to your room, where you practise stances until dinner.

events.text: One of your family's caravan guards, a scarred old man, catches you watching him practise at dawn.

ok.log: He grunts. Then, every dawn for a year, he shows you one movement. Just one. It is enough to begin.

fail.log: 'Go back to your abacus, little master.' You copy him from behind the woodpile anyway.

choices.text: Tell your father he is slacking

effects.log: He is dismissed. You get five taels and a strange, heavy feeling in your chest.

events.text: Your cousins in the main branch call you 'the side-branch weed' and push you into the koi pond.

choices.text: Climb out and fight all three

ok.log: All three end up in the pond. The family elders pretend not to see, and one of them smiles.

fail.log: You end up back in the pond, twice. You learn exactly how cold the water is.

choices.text: Stay in the pond until they get bored

effects.log: You watch the koi. They move without effort, bending around every push. You think about that for years.

events.text: The family library is forbidden to children. The door, however, is not locked.

ok.log: You read by moonlight until your eyes burn. Some of it stays. More than it should.

fail.log: Caught by the librarian. Your punishment is copying the family rules one hundred times. You learn them very well.

effects.log: You walk past the door every day for five years. It never gets less tempting.

events.text: The old abbot of the temple that raised you makes you carry water up the mountain every day. Two buckets. No complaints.

choices.text: Carry it without spilling a drop

effects.log: It takes two years before you stop spilling. The abbot never praises you. He does start giving you bigger buckets.
'So your legs learn before your head does,' he says. It makes no sense. Years later it makes perfect sense.

events.text: In a hungry winter, the temple has one bowl of rice left and four children.

choices.text: Give your share to the youngest

effects.log: You go to bed hungry. The youngest follows you around like a duckling for the rest of the winter.
You eat. Nobody blames you. You remember the youngest's face anyway.

events.text: The older street kids want you to pick a noble's pocket as your 'initiation'.

ok.log: Smooth as silk. The gang accepts you. The noble never notices. You notice for weeks.

fail.log: The noble's guard catches your wrist. You escape with bruises and a lesson in humility.

effects.log: They push you around for a month. Then one of them, quietly, starts walking away too.

events.text: A filthy old beggar under the bridge watches you steal a bun and says: 'Your footwork is terrible. Sit down.'

effects.log: He teaches you to breathe 'like a sleeping dog'. It sounds ridiculous. Your body feels warm for the first time in years.
He does not chase you. Years later, you still wonder who he was.

events.text: In the ashes of your family's old hall, you dig up a rusted sword with a name carved on the hilt. Your grandfather goes pale when he sees it.

effects.log: 'That was your great-grandfather's,' he says finally. 'He died holding it.' You clean it every night after that.
Some things should sleep. Your grandfather nods, and for once, he hugs you.

events.text: At the harvest festival, a travelling troupe performs a 'martial arts show'. One of them clearly knows real kung fu.

ok.log: He notices you and shows you one real stance, 'so you know the difference'. You practise it for a year.

fail.log: You lose him in the crowd. You spend the whole festival looking.

effects.log: Dumplings, lanterns, fireworks. One perfect night of being a child.

events.text: You wander too far chasing a rabbit and night falls. The forest is very dark and very loud.

choices.text: Climb a tree and wait for morning

effects.log: A long, cold night. At dawn you find your way home by the smoke from the cooking fires.

ok.log: Water always finds people. You walk into the village before midnight, muddy and very proud.

fail.log: You slip down a bank in the dark. A woodcutter finds you at dawn, cold and scraped.

events.text: An old fisherman by the river never seems to catch anything. One day he tells you it is because he is not trying to.

effects.log: You sit with him every afternoon. You learn patience. He learns you talk too much. You both improve.

choices.text: Show him how to actually fish

effects.log: You catch six fish in an hour. He laughs so hard he nearly falls in the river.

events.text: {npc} challenges you to race up the hill behind the village. The loser has to carry the winner's water for a month.

mem.note: beat me in the hill race

ok.log: You win by a step. {npc} carries your water for a month, glaring the whole time.

fail.log: {npc} wins. You carry the water. Your legs get very strong.

effects.log: You are a child. {npc} points this out loudly for a week.

events.text: Someone broke the village headman's window. Everyone saw {npc} do it. {npc} is telling everyone it was you.

mem.note: got me punished for the window

ok.log: The headman believes you. {npc} spends a week cleaning the shrine.

fail.log: Nobody believes you. You spend a week cleaning the shrine and planning revenge.

mem.note: took the blame for my window

effects.log: You clean the shrine. {npc} watches from the fence, confused. Later, a stolen peach appears on your windowsill.

events.text: {npc} shows you a hidden cave behind the waterfall. 'Our secret sect,' {he} says. 'We need a name.'

mem.note: founded the Invincible Heaven-Shaking Sect with me

effects.log: It has two members, one wooden sword and a jar of dried persimmons. It is the greatest sect in the world.

mem.note: named our secret sect after us

effects.log: {npc} pretends it is a stupid name. {He} carves it into the rock the next day.

events.text: {npc}'s family is moving to the capital. {He} gives you {his} most precious possession: a chipped wooden horse.

mem.note: gave me a keepsake when I left

effects.log: You give {him} your lucky stone. 'We'll meet again in the murim,' {he} says. You believe it.
You promise. The capital is very far away, but promises are longer.

events.text: Three older boys are tormenting a stray puppy behind the rice mill.

ok.log: You win, somehow. The puppy follows you home and refuses to leave. It is yours now.

fail.log: You lose badly, but the puppy escapes while they are busy with you. Worth it.

effects.log: The miller's wife arrives with a broom. Nobody torments anything for a very long time.
You hear it yelping all the way home.

events.text: A fortune teller at the temple fair reads your palm, gasps, and refuses to take your money.

choices.text: Demand to know what she saw

effects.log: 'Great fortune,' she whispers. 'Or great trouble. Honestly, the lines are very smudged. Wash your hands.'

choices.text: Keep your coin, and leave quickly

effects.log: You buy a candied hawthorn with the savings. Fate can wait.

events.text: You build a kite shaped like a crane. On its first flight, the wind takes it over the mountain.

effects.log: You watch it until it is a dot, then nothing. For years you imagine it landing somewhere wonderful.

events.text: A winter fever takes hold of you. For three days you burn and dream of a white tiger walking through clouds.

choices.text: Tell the healer about the dream

effects.log: The healer goes quiet, then lights incense. You recover. The dream never quite leaves.
You recover. Sometimes, falling asleep, you can still hear the tiger breathing.

events.text: You build a wooden training dummy out of fence posts and hit it every day until your knuckles bleed.

effects.log: The dummy breaks first. You build a sturdier one.

choices.text: Wrap your hands and train smarter

effects.log: Slower progress. Fewer scars. You notice the difference.

events.text: A famous swordsman rides through the village. When he stops to water his horse, every child crowds around him. He looks at you.

effects.log: 'Wake up earlier than everyone who wants the same thing,' he says, and rides away. You wake up before the roosters for a year.
He laughs and lets you. It is colder and heavier than you imagined. You dream about it for weeks.

events.text: You try to meditate like the heroes in the stories. Within a minute, a fly lands on your nose.

choices.text: Ignore it like a true master

ok.log: You sit through the fly, a bee and a curious goat. You feel something shift inside. Also, the goat eats your sandal.

fail.log: You last three seconds, then slap yourself in the face. The fly survives.

effects.log: An hour later, sweating, you declare a truce. The fly has won.

events.text: The neighbour's rooster attacks you every single morning on your way to the well.

effects.log: It always strikes from the left, low. You learn to dodge. It learns to feint. You both get better.
The whole village watches. It is a draw. The rooster considers you a worthy rival from then on.

events.text: The village teacher catches you drawing sword stances in the margins of your Analects.

effects.log: He sighs. 'At least draw them correctly,' he says, and fixes your elbow angle with his brush.

choices.text: Explain that these are more useful than the Analects

effects.log: He makes you copy the Analects twice. But he keeps the drawing.

events.text: On the night of your birthday, the same comet that marked your birth returns. You cannot sleep. Your body hums.

effects.log: By morning, something inside you has woken. You do not have a word for it yet.

events.text: A wounded fox kit stumbles into your yard and lets only you come near it.

effects.log: It heals, leaves, and comes back every spring with something shiny in its mouth. Once, it is a silver ring.
The healer fixes its leg. It follows you around for a week, then disappears into the hills.

events.text: The town is holding a dumpling-eating contest. The prize: a real iron sword.

ok.log: Forty-two dumplings. A new town record. You cannot move for a day. You sell the sword to a real swordsman for thirty taels.

fail.log: You are beaten by a grandmother who eats like a machine. She gives you a dumpling out of pity.

effects.log: The hardest battle of your childhood, fought entirely inside yourself.

events.text: The only way to the sect recruitment fair is across a rope bridge over a gorge. It sways.

ok.log: You make it. You open your eyes on the other side and realise you were brave for about forty steps.

fail.log: You freeze halfway. A kind old woman walks you across, holding your hand. Nobody ever speaks of it.

effects.log: Three extra days of walking. You arrive late, tired and completely alive.
